title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: No winner invented when resources tie
summary: Hovering a resource defined in several modules named a winner and struck the others through. When two definitions carry the same priority, that winner was only whichever file the index had scanned first.

highlights.title: Tied definitions are shown as tied
highlights.description: Two libraries both in main, or two exclusive build variants of one module, carry the same priority. The hover now lists them side by side and says that the Gradle dependency order settles it.

highlights.title: Nothing struck out by mistake
highlights.description: Measured on a real project: of 122 shadowing hovers, 20 named an arbitrary winner. The remaining 102 keep their winner, and no hover was lost along the way.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The priority score knows two things: app against library, and main against another source set. Definitions that land on the same number are no longer ranked against each other.
A duplicate sitting in the very same folder keeps its Android merge error label. It shares the top score, so it would otherwise have dropped out of the list entirely.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: No command or setting changes in this release. The work sits entirely in the resource shadowing hover.
